the effect of spatial complexity on visual working memory in persons with different levels of autistic-like traits.
how the self-reported autistic-like trait influences the capacity of visual short-term memory, and how this trait is related to the spatial configuration of visual stimuli.

spatial configuration is not an important component for visual working memory in individuals with a higher level of self-reported autistic-like features.
the capacity of visual short-term memory in persons with high AQ scores was less influenced by the complexity of the visual stimuli.

self-rated autistic-like traits affect the capacity of visual short-term memory for complex configurations, but not for simple ones.

self-reported autistic-like characteristics may affect the capacity of visual short term memory in a way that is not related to the capacity itself.
